text: The system shall hold each declared class of action, and whether that class needs the authorization of the user.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 makes the platform tell the difference between an action that needs the authorization of the user and an action that does not, and a difference that no declaration states cannot be told. DEC-116 makes this system the one holder, because a class that each boundary keeps for itself becomes one policy for each boundary (DEC-019). MET-005 keeps the store out of the statement. The first text held only a class that needs the authorization of the user. REQ-AU-020 and DEC-109 add a class that states that an act needs none.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a class, a change to a class and the removal of a class from an agent only.
rationale: REQ-PL-028 accepts a declaration from an agent only, and DEC-115 gives the reason: to structure a statement of the user into a declaration is a judgement, and DEC-030 keeps a judgement out of the platform. DEC-054 states that the reason of DEC-025 does not carry to a class, because an agent that declares a class also changes one. REQ-PL-028 states a declaration and a change to a declaration, and DEC-055 removes a class by the path that declared it, so all three name the same writer and rule 1 keeps them in one row.

text: The system shall not accept the declaration of a class, or a change to a class, until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that declaration or that change.
rationale: DEC-054. The gate on the class register is stated here and is not an entry in the register, because a gate that is an entry cannot be read when the register is empty and the first class could not then be declared. DEC-049 keeps the record out of this system, so the requirement states that the platform records the answer and does not state where. A change to a class narrows it as readily as it widens it, and a narrowed class makes an action silent, so the change passes the same gate. The removal is REQ-AU-014, under REQ-PL-013.

text: The system shall give, for an act that a caller called and the arguments of that act, whether that act is in a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-012 needs the difference to be told before the action, and DEC-019 declares in one place and refuses in many, so this system answers and the caller refuses. The object is part of the question because a class of REQ-PL-013 cannot be judged from the action alone: to send a message to the user and to send a message to a third party are one action with two objects. DEC-057 makes the act exist before the request, so the caller states an action that it prepared and not a description of one that it intends. The answer crosses the boundary of this system, so MET-018 holds it in a row and the type is interface. OPN-025 states the norm that two rows follow, out and back. The first text said an action and its object. DEC-103 judges the act with its arguments, and the class of REQ-PL-013 that commits funds reads the amount and the payee, which are not one object.

text: The system shall accept from Actuation an act that the caller called and the arguments of that act.
rationale: REQ-AU-004 cannot answer without both. MET-018 needs the contract to be held by a row that both sides name, and DEC-111 makes Actuation the one caller that asks, so REQ-AC-013 is the supplier. DEC-057 makes the act exist before the request. The first text said an action and its object, which INT-PL-17 no longer states.

text: The system shall give the declared classes to a caller.
rationale: REQ-PL-027 makes the rules for work with the platform agree with what the platform refuses. DEC-069 makes that agreement hold without a copy: the rules state that a declaration bounds what the platform accepts (REQ-AD-046) and carry no content (REQ-AD-047), and a caller reads the classes here at the moment that it needs them. Two statements of one register drift, which is the failure that DEC-019 states. This is an obligation at the interface and not a capability of this system, so FUN-AU-01 generates it and no third function is written. INT-PL-22 carries it to Actuation, which holds the act that gives the classes.

text: When the system cannot decide whether an action is in a declared class, the system shall give that the action is in a declared class.
rationale: RSK-AU-001 is the failure where an action that needed the user occurs with no answer, and REQ-PL-013 names actions that no person can reverse. A gate that passes what it cannot judge is not a gate. The cost is RSK-AU-002: the user is asked about actions that no class needed. The user accepts that cost while the set of declared acts is small, because an agent that reads the work that closed finds the actions that the system could not decide and proposes a class that covers them.

text: The system shall not answer a classification from a statement of the declared classes other than the statement that it gives to a caller.
rationale: RSK-AU-004. REQ-AU-006 gives the declared classes to a caller, and DEC-069 keeps that the only statement of them: REQ-AD-047 refuses a copy in the rules for work with the platform. Two statements of the same classes drift, which is the failure that DEC-019 states, and a caller cannot see the difference from outside. This row refuses the system answering from any statement but the one it gives.

text: The system shall answer a classification within TBD.
rationale: Each act on the outside world waits for this answer before it proceeds (DEC-111), so this system is on the path of every such act, as REQ-AD-015 is for a position. The value depends on the host and on which boundary asks: a boundary on a conversational path and a boundary in scheduled work do not need the same number, and neither is known. REQ-AD-015 and REQ-ST-028 carry the same TBD for the same reason. RSK-AU-006 is the failure that this answers.

text: The system shall hold, with each declared class, the writer that declared it.
rationale: REQ-ST-031 holds the writer with each declared kind for the same reason. DEC-056 makes the platform state the origin of a record, REQ-PL-029 is its product requirement, and DEC-061 makes the writer the part of the origin that the platform states. Without the writer nobody can see which agent proposed a class, and RSK-AU-005 and RSK-AU-008 are both failures that a reader finds only by reading it.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a class, a change to a class and the removal of a class from a caller whose position does not admit the act.
rationale: REQ-ST-032, REQ-WC-023 and REQ-AD-019 state the same refusal at the other declaration boundaries, and this system stated none, so any caller that reached it declared a class. DEC-019 makes each boundary refuse and DEC-029 makes the declaration of a class an act. REQ-PL-005 keeps an agent inside the authority that its position gives.

text: The system shall give the declared classes after the platform stops and starts.
rationale: REQ-AD-007 states the same observable for what states an agent. REQ-PL-012 cannot tell the difference between an action that needs the user and one that does not when the classes are gone, and REQ-AU-008 then answers that every action is in a declared class. A class that the user already answered for is not asked again.

text: The system shall not accept the removal of a class until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that removal.
rationale: REQ-PL-013 names three classes that the user states as a hard boundary. DEC-055 makes no class permanent, so the platform does not keep the three by refusing to remove them. An earlier row in this system stated that refusal and was deleted under MET-024, because a system that obeys REQ-AU-002 and DEC-055 cannot guarantee that it holds the three. What the platform owes REQ-PL-013 is that no class is lost without an answer of the user. That the user is not told afterwards is RSK-AU-003.

text: The system shall give a copy of the declared classes that is of a state that the system held at one time.
rationale: REQ-AD-036 states the same for what states an agent. REQ-PL-022 names the declared classes, and DEC-020 gives the holder of a body the copy and the decision of when to make it, and gives External Access the carriage only. DEC-116 makes this system their one holder, so no other compartment can state what a consistent copy of them is. OPN-040 reaches this row.

text: The system shall restore the declared classes from a copy that it gave.
rationale: REQ-AD-037 states the same for what states an agent. Rule 1 keeps the copy and the restoration apart, as Agent Definition already does. REQ-PL-022 names the declared classes, and DEC-020 gives the holder of a body the copy and the decision of when to make it, and gives External Access the carriage only. DEC-116 makes this system their one holder, so no other compartment can state what a consistent copy of them is. OPN-040 reaches this row.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of a class of action that needs the authorization of the user, and of a class that states that an act needs none.
rationale: REQ-PL-031. REQ-AU-001 holds each declared class, REQ-AU-002 constrains the writer and REQ-AU-003 refuses the act until the user answers. None of the three states that the system accepts the act, so the one register that REQ-PL-013 rests on had no requirement that a class can be made at all. The first text accepted only a class that needs the authorization of the user. REQ-AU-020 and DEC-109 add a class that states that an act needs none, and REQ-AU-003 gates it in the same way.

text: The system shall accept a change to a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-031. REQ-AU-003 refuses the change until the platform records an affirmative answer, which gates an act that nothing stated.

text: The system shall accept the removal of a declared class.
rationale: REQ-PL-031, DEC-055 and DEC-071. REQ-AU-014 refuses the removal until the platform records an affirmative answer, and DEC-055 states that no class is permanent, so the act was reasoned about and never stated. No declaration depends on a class.

text: The system shall give that an act on the outside world is in a declared class unless a declared class states that the act needs no authorization of the user.
rationale: DEC-109. A declared act on the outside world that no class names was answered as in no class, so an act that a new service offers reached the outside world with no answer of the user, and REQ-AU-008 did not catch it because the answer was decidable. REQ-PL-013 names acts that nobody can reverse. A class that states that an act needs no authorization is declared as any class is, so REQ-AU-003 gates the exemption and the user answers for it once.

text: The system shall give the caller, with each refusal of an act that has no affirmative answer of the user, that the act needs an affirmative answer of the user.
rationale: DEC-104 has a boundary refuse and the caller raise the request. DEC-054 keeps the gate of this system out of the class register, and Actuation does not classify an act inside the platform (DEC-111) and carries it here, and the refusal of REQ-AU-003 or REQ-AU-014 is the only point at which the caller learns that the act needs an answer. The first text named only a class. DEC-114 gates the parties in the same way.

text: The system shall give whether any declared class that states that an act needs no authorization names a given act on the outside world.
rationale: REQ-AC-035 refuses a change to a declared act that a class names, and only this system holds the classes. REQ-AD-053 gives the same for a position. A class that gates an act does not block a change to it, so only an exemption is given. The first text gave any class.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of a class that states that an act on the outside world needs no authorization unless the class names each act that it covers.
rationale: DEC-109. An exemption stated as a condition over every act covers an act that is declared or changed after the user approved it, which is the path around REQ-PL-013 that REQ-AC-035 closes for a named act. An exemption may still state a condition over the arguments of an act that it names.

text: The system shall accept a call of a caller to an act that it holds, and a released gated unit whose act it holds, only from Actuation, with the caller or the raiser that Actuation states.
rationale: DEC-111 and OPN-085. A call from elsewhere is a path around Actuation, and a caller read from the call is a position that the caller chose. REQ-AC-027 states the caller. REQ-AC-026 carries a released gated unit with its raiser.

text: The system shall give Actuation the result of each call and each released gated unit that Actuation carried to it.
rationale: DEC-111. The caller waits on its call to Actuation, and the result returns on that call (REQ-AC-011). A released gated unit has no caller that waits, and Actuation gives its result to Work and Coordination (REQ-AC-020). OPN-079.

text: The system shall refuse a released gated unit whose act the position of its raiser does not admit.
rationale: DEC-048: a yes is not a change to what a position admits. REQ-AC-028 covers the acts that Actuation holds, and the holder of an act inside the platform covers its own. Without this row an agent raises a unit for an act that its position does not admit, and the answer of the user does the act.

text: The system shall accept the declaration of the parties that count as the user, a change to them and their removal.
rationale: REQ-PL-031 and DEC-114. The parties are a declaration, and each declaration has a path through an agent.

text: The system shall not accept the declaration of the parties that count as the user, or a change to them, until the platform records an affirmative answer to a request that states that declaration or that change, with each party as the system will hold it.
rationale: DEC-114. To add a party makes each message to it silent, which is the effect of a change to a class (REQ-AU-003). A removal makes more acts gated and needs no answer. The request states each party as it will be held (DEC-104), so the user approves what the platform holds.

text: The system shall judge a condition of a class over the recipient of an act against the declared parties that count as the user.
rationale: DEC-114 and OPN-084. REQ-PL-013 gates a message to a third party and not a message to the user, and the arguments of an act name a recipient but not whether it is the user.

text: The system shall refuse the declaration of the parties that count as the user, a change to them and their removal from a caller whose position does not admit the act.
rationale: DEC-019 and DEC-114. REQ-AU-012 states the same refusal for a class. Without this row any agent removes a party, and each message to the user is gated.
